questions.question: Discuss the role of Vitamin A in vision and growth
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Vitamin A in vision – (3 marks)
  •  Retinol is oxidized to retinal which combines with opsin to produce rhodopsin-(1mark)
  •  When light strikes the retina, the rod cells are bleached, rhodopsin splits to form
  • retinal and opsin and nerve stimulus is transmitted to the visual centre of the brain
  • where the sensation of vision is created-(2 marks)
  • Role of vitamin A in growth-(2 marks)
  •  Vitamin A, is essential for normal growth and development-(1 mark)
  •  Vitamin A deficiency leads to loss of appetite, followed by a cessation of growth then
  • rapid weight loss and ultimate death- (1 mark)
questions.final_answer: rapid weight loss and ultimate death

questions.question: Discuss the role of Vitamin C in collagen synthesis
questions.solution_html:
• Role of vitamin C in collagen synthesis – (5 marks)
  •  Vitamin C is required by the fibroblasts and the bone forming osteoblasts within bone.
  • – (1 mark)
  •  Any deficiency in vitamin C results in defective collagen synthesis, associated with
  • impaired wound healing. - (1 mark)
  •  If collagen synthesis is impaired, the matrix formation is defective and it becomes less
  • able to accumulate the calcium and phosphorus required for proper bone
  • mineralisation. - (1 mark)
  •  The bone becomes weakened and sometimes distorted ((1 mark))
  •  Bones sometimes become displaced from their joints when the supporting cartilage
  • which is also mainly collagen, becomes weakened. - (1 mark)

questions.question: Summarize unsaturated fatty acids.
questions.solution_html:
• Summarize unsaturated fatty acids
  • Unsaturated fatty acids - An unsaturated fat is a fat or fatty acid in which there is at least
  • one double bond within the fatty acid chain. ((1 Mark))
  • Example
  • Monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA): A fatty acid chain is monounsaturated if it contains
  • one double bond. Eg- Oleic acid ((0.5 mark))
  • Polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA): A fatty acid is polyunsaturated if it contains more than
  • one double bond. They are of 2 types- Omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids. ((0.5 mark))
questions.final_answer: one double bond. They are of 2 types- Omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids. ()

questions.question: Discuss soft diet. / Part D Long essay Questions
questions.solution_html:
•  It is the second most common hospital diet. It bridges the gap between acute illness
  • and convalescence. ((1 mark))
  •  It may be used in acute infections, following surgery, and for patients who are unable
  • to chew. The diet is made up of simple, easily digestible food and contains no harsh
  • fibre, low in fat and no rich highly seasoned food. ((1 mark))
  •  It is nutritionally adequate when planned on the basis of normal diet. Three meals with
  • intermediate feedings are given in this diet. The diet provides 1500kcal and 35-40 g
  • protein. ((1 mark))
  • Mechanical soft diet is given for patients who have difficulty in chewing. It is limited to soft
  • foods. ((0.5 marks))
  • Fibre restricted soft diet differs from normal diet in being reduced in fibre content and soft
  • in consistency. ((0.5 marks))
  • Foods included are well cooked cereals, bread, ice-cream, milk, yoghurt, poached egg
  • mashed potato, fruits, pudding, soups etc. ((0.5 marks))
  • Foods avoided are desserts like rich puddings and cakes, dried fruits and nuts, fried foods
  • highly seasoned soups, raw vegetables, spices and bran of cereals. ((0.5 marks))
  • Essay Type Questions

questions.question: Discuss the roles of Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), Specific Dynamic Action (SDA), / Physical Activity Level (PAL) and total energy expenditure (TEE) in nutritional planning and weight management strategies.
questions.solution_html:
• Management strategies.
  •  BMR- Definition – (1 Mark)
  •  Forms the foundation of energy requirement calculations - (0.5 Marks)
  •  Helps determine the minimum calorie intake needed to sustain life- 0.5
  • Marks
  •  Individuals with higher BMR require more calories; those with lower BMR need fewer
  • (0.5Marks)
  •  Knowing BMR helps create calorie deficits for weight loss or surpluses for weight gain
  • safely- (0.5 Marks)
  •  SDA- Definition – (1 Mark)
  •  Contributes to overall calorie burn; protein-rich foods have a higher SDA, which can slightly
  • increase energy expenditure- (0.5 Marks)
  •  Important in planning balanced diet for weight management. - (0.5 Marks)
  •  Aids in understanding how meal frequency and food choices influence metabolism. - 0.5
  • Marks
  •  PAL - Definition – (1 Mark)
  •  The most variable part of energy expenditure; crucial for customizing diet plans. - 0.5
  • Marks
  •  Higher PAL increases energy needs, essential for athletes or active individuals. - (0.5 Marks)
  •  Enables dietitians to tailor activity recommendations—walking, exercise routines, or lifestyle
  • modifications. - (0.5 Marks)
  •  TEE- Definition – (1 Mark)
  •  Helps to determine whether a person should consume: Less than TEE → for weight
  • loss, Equal to TEE → for weight maintenance, More than TEE → for weight gain- 0.5
  • Marks
  •  Essential for calculating precise caloric targets based on age, sex, body composition, health
  • status, and lifestyle- (0.5 Marks)
